severity_scope: Trusted-operator local development profile; no CVSS score or security certification claimed.

findings.title: Unscoped berth lifecycle paths
findings.evidence: Baseline unload with ../outside deleted an isolated sibling directory.
findings.repair: Validate names and resolve contained paths before berth operations. Reject links/reparse points and unsafe components.
findings.residual: The host filesystem and cooperating operator remain trusted; not race-proof against a privileged concurrent writer.

findings.title: Destructive replacement before admission
findings.evidence: Baseline replacement with a nonexistent source removed the existing isolated berth.
findings.repair: Stage, verify and swap; retain the previous generation; attempt rollback on ordinary pre-commit failure.
findings.validation: Missing-source, staged failure, swap failure and journal fault tests.
findings.residual: Cross-resource recovery spanning registry, seal, hull and TIFF state remains partial.

findings.title: ZIP admission and cross-platform loss hazards
findings.evidence: Archive extraction had no explicit count/expanded-size/ratio policy and no complete duplicate/special-entry admission. Ordinary extractall sanitization is not claimed universally vulnerable to traversal.
findings.repair: Preflight canonical members, limits, encryption, links, duplicates and file/directory conflicts; stream flat staged blobs before portable aliasing.
findings.validation: Archive rejection suite and actual eight-file ZIP/native integration.
findings.residual: Native payloads are still trusted; the input budget is not a global storage or CPU quota.

findings.title: Slot-run bypasses ledger identity and failure result
findings.evidence: A supplied path could bypass intended cargo lookup; alias/wrong-slot and native failure handling were insufficient.
findings.repair: Require a unique ledger entry in the requested slot, contained path, matching size and digest; propagate failed native halts.
findings.validation: Original-path and alias resolution, wrong-slot, untracked, modified-byte and failed-result tests.
findings.residual: A registered file is not proof its behavior is safe; real guest isolation remains absent.

findings.title: Sealed result does not enforce its pinned witness
findings.evidence: Sealed success did not consistently require matches_pinned or a valid pre-execution reference contract.
findings.repair: Validate parsed program seal, row count and witness before execution; require the pinned match in the final result.
findings.validation: Actual successful native run, then deliberately changed reference plus recomputed file sums is refused with exit 3.
findings.residual: These checks cover the executed witness program, not arbitrary cargo-language semantics.

findings.title: Incomplete pin and checksum admission
findings.evidence: Missing hold pins and malformed checksum records could be accepted or confused with host limitations.
findings.repair: Require all five hold pins, reject malformed/duplicate/escaping checksum records and preserve parser failures as failures.
findings.validation: Missing-pin, invalid digest, duplicate, traversal and strict parser tests; full rebuild and native gates.
findings.residual: A local hash is not an independently authenticated publisher signature; mutable caches remain a trust boundary.

findings.title: Hull reassembly paths and mount ownership
findings.evidence: Reassembly and mount names lacked consistent path confinement and ownership protections; corrupt registry could silently appear empty.
findings.repair: Constrain paths/names, verify cargo bytes, reject unowned replacement and unreadable registry; write ownership atomically.
findings.validation: Mount ownership and registry corruption regression tests; full hull and face integration.
findings.residual: Carried-key enrollment is operator trust, not external release authorization; full transactional mount rollback is not implemented.

findings.title: Tick success overstates executed agreement
findings.evidence: Success could overlook required hull/replay/mount/native outcomes.
findings.repair: Require participating engine, fabric, requested hull and requested mount execution, pinned agreement and replay success for TICK_OK.
findings.validation: Native B10 differential, chained, painted-tick and painted-declaration cases across all six delivered berths.
findings.residual: Agreement is local deterministic execution, not fault-independent consensus or workload correctness.

findings.title: Manifest inventory inconsistencies
findings.evidence: Inventory verification did not comprehensively enforce duplicate entries, counts and aggregate bytes.
findings.repair: Validate entry identity, size/hash, file count, total bytes and absence of extra included files; reject included nonregular filesystem objects.
findings.residual: Duplicate-key-safe JSON and complete canonical schema migrations are still roadmap work.

findings.title: Stale berth inventory after final unload
findings.evidence: Empty berth lists could leave old manifest berth metadata in place.
findings.repair: Always rewrite berth list, even when empty, and current release identity on reseal.
findings.validation: Last-berth reseal regression; final package inventory verification.
findings.residual: Historical seal lineage is preserved and intentionally retains older release evidence.

findings.title: Checksum self-reference in new berth metadata
findings.evidence: BERTH.json attempted to retain a digest of the sums file that subsequently binds BERTH.json.
findings.repair: Omit this circular field in newly generated BERTH.json; bind current sums externally in the bill of lading.
findings.validation: New-load integration verifies no self-reference and valid berth sums.
findings.residual: Historical delivered berth artifacts are retained byte-for-byte, not silently rewritten.

findings.title: Concurrent mutation and truncated writes
findings.evidence: Independent writers and direct metadata/image replacement risk interleaving or truncating state.
findings.repair: Serialize cooperating commands with an OS-released lock and use same-directory fsync/replace for core metadata and ship TIFF updates.
findings.validation: Multiprocess lock contention; atomic write failures preserve prior bytes.
findings.residual: No all-resource commit protocol or arbitrary host-writer protection; some diagnostic output files remain direct writes.

findings.title: Invalid numeric inputs and weak CLI error contracts
findings.evidence: Negative, enormous or non-finite inputs and inconsistent errors could produce misleading behavior.
findings.repair: Bound ticks/scale/interval/steps; restrict program names; emit stable nonzero error categories with diagnostic logs and preserve interrupts.
findings.residual: No externally versioned management API, full subprocess supervision or universal deadline contract yet.

findings.title: Windows path and generated-namespace collisions
findings.evidence: Case/normalization differences, Windows device names, long paths and cargo metadata names could overwrite or obstruct generated content.
findings.repair: Preserve logical names in a ledger; alias portable collisions and generated namespaces; quote Windows launch paths and retain exit status.
findings.validation: Case-pair, AUX, long-path, CARGO_MANIFEST case-pair and _Alias integration with all original bytes intact; static package path checks.
findings.residual: Native Windows and macOS execution has not been observed; runtime toolchains and root path length still matter.

findings.title: Unbounded TIFF history and partial writes
findings.evidence: Append/read operations lacked explicit ship-level byte/page/geometry/sidecar budgets.
findings.repair: Enforce 8 MiB, 512 pages, fixed raster and bounded sidecar on ship-managed state; atomically replace files and close frames.
findings.validation: Real Pillow codec append/read/limit/error-preservation tests and native B9/B10.
findings.residual: Embedded hull decoder entry points, initial allocation, rollover, global disk quotas and multi-picture atomicity remain incomplete.

findings.title: Top-level PASS can hide nested skipped coverage
findings.evidence: The inherited ship summary can show no skips while nested berth gates are skipped for absent sample types.
findings.repair: Add --require-complete, recursively refusing any SKIPPED gate, with failure taking precedence.
findings.validation: Four result-policy tests; actual full verification preserves all nested skip evidence.
findings.residual: This is deliberately conservative, not a required/optional/not-applicable production qualification classifier.

findings.title: Missing real unikernel execution and independent trust boundary
findings.locations: Architecture; guest backend; host runtime; release process
findings.evidence: No bootable guest, hypervisor isolation, OS-enforced deny-network, multi-tenant identity, external release authentication or multi-host consensus was identified.
findings.repair: Document actual capability limits in doctor, SECURITY.md and the 96-item theory-derived roadmap. No simulated completion claims.
findings.validation: Local capability report explicitly reports these features false.
findings.residual: Requires new guest/build/isolation/lifecycle/security components; UC-2.2.0 remains a trusted local skeleton.
